tz_requirements.text: Authentication and authorization.
Landing page.
Creating workspaces and inviting members. One user can belong to several workspaces.
Roles and access rights. At minimum owner, administrator and member.
Ability to remove a member from the workspace, change their role and revoke an invitation.
Creating projects inside a workspace. For example, a team develops a website and a mobile app at the same time.
A project must have a description, members, communication channels, tasks and a linked GitHub repository.
Creating public and private channels. Public channels are available to project members; private ones require a separate invitation.
Editing a channel's name and description, archiving channels.
Think through who can create projects, invite members and manage channels.
Direct messages between workspace members, group conversations and project channels.
Sending and receiving messages in real time.
Basic formatting: text emphasis, lists, links and code blocks.
Editing and deleting your own messages. An edited message must carry a corresponding mark.
Discussion threads under messages. Replies in a thread must be separate from the main conversation.
Reactions to messages.
User mentions with a notification.
Pinned messages and saving messages to a personal favorites list.
Sending images and files. Images need a preview.
Message search + filters by project, channel, author and date.
Paginated loading of message history when scrolling up.
Unread message counters and a separate display of mentions.
Ability to jump to the first unread message.
Member presence statuses and a typing indicator.
Connection recovery. If a user loses internet, they must receive the missed messages after reconnecting.
Message sending state. If a message failed to send, the user must see an error and be able to retry.
Ability to create a task from a message. For example, a bug is found in a discussion, so the message is turned into a task right away.
Ability to create a task on its own, without a source message.
A task must have an identifier, title, description, assignee, author, status, priority, due date and checklist.
When a task is created from a message, a link to the source discussion is saved.
A message shows that a task was created from it. You can go to the task and see its current status.
Ability to attach files and related messages to a task.
Task discussion in a separate thread. It must be accessible both from the task card and from the channel.
Ability to mention a task in a message and go to it.
Task change history: who changed the status, due date, description or assignee.
Every project has a Kanban board.
Base statuses: "To do", "In progress", "In review", "Done".
Ability to configure columns and move tasks between them.
Preserving the order of tasks within columns.
Filters by assignee, priority and due date.
All changes on the board are visible to members in real time.
Ability to mark a task as blocked and give a reason. For example, "waiting for the API from the backend".
When a task is assigned, its due date approaches or a blocker appears, the responsible people receive a notification.
A personal "My Work" section that gathers the user's tasks from all projects, review requests and mentions.
Ability to connect a GitHub repository to a project and choose a channel for notifications. For the first version, one repository per project is enough.
A repository must be connected by a user with the appropriate rights. Tokens and secrets must not end up in the frontend or in messages.
Notifications about PR opened, review requested, CI result and merge.
Ability to link a task to a PR. For example, by putting the task identifier in the PR description or attaching a link manually.
The task card shows linked PRs and their state.
A PR message shows the author, title, link and check results.
Ability to configure simple rules: PR opened — the task moves to "In review", PR merged — "Done".
Automatic transitions must be visible in the task history. Think through the behavior when several PRs are linked to a task.
Redelivery of the same webhook must not create duplicate messages or repeat actions.
Verifying the authenticity of incoming webhooks is mandatory.
Information from a private repository must be available only to members who are allowed access to it. Connecting a repository must not automatically expose its contents to the whole workspace.
The project administrator configures the schedule, time zone and standup questions.
For example: "What did you do?", "What are you planning?", "What is blocking you?".
At the scheduled time, members receive a reminder to fill in the report.
Links to tasks and PRs can be added to an answer.
Answers are collected in a single discussion per day.
It is visible who has already answered and who has not yet.
The report history is available to project members.
AI compiles a short summary: what has progressed, what blockers there are and who needs help. The summary must include links to members' answers.
Ability to save a message or thread as a team decision.
A decision has a title, description, author, date and a link to the source discussion.
Decisions are collected in a separate project tab.
Ability to replace a decision with a new one, preserving the history and an explanation of the changes.
A decision can be linked to tasks.
AI can suggest a draft decision based on a discussion. A member saves it after reviewing it.
A short recap of a discussion that was missed.
Answers to questions based on the messages, tasks and decisions available to the user. For example: "Why did we decide to use this library?" or "What is blocking the release right now?".
Answers with links to the source data.
Suggesting tasks based on the outcome of a discussion. The user reviews titles, descriptions and assignees before creation.
A project summary: completed tasks, open blockers and PRs waiting for review.
Preparing a draft weekly report from standups, tasks and GitHub events.
If there is not enough information, the AI must say so.
Access rights are mandatory: it must not be possible to obtain the contents of a private channel, repository or someone else's project through the AI.
Generation must have a clear state: in progress, completed or failed.
AI output must not automatically change tasks, publish decisions or send messages on the user's behalf without their confirmation.
Think separately about how to use AI inside the application. It must work with conversations and project data: helping to find information, understand context and collect the results of discussions.
Personal account and settings.
A unified notification center: mentions, assigned tasks, replies in discussions and review requests.
Ability to go from a notification to the specific message, task or PR.
Notification settings for individual channels and projects.
"Do not disturb" mode and working hours that take the time zone into account.
Telegram bot integration: reminders about standups, assigned tasks, mentions and review requests.
Reading a notification in one tab must update its state in the other tabs.
Think through which notifications to send immediately, which to defer, and how not to flood the user with identical messages.
Voice rooms inside channels.
Ability to join a conversation, mute the microphone and leave.
Showing the room's participants and who is speaking right now.
Screen sharing.
Access rights check on joining. Outsiders must not get into the room of a private channel.
Handling connection loss, denied microphone access and the end of screen sharing.
During a conversation, you can open a related task and discuss it together with the team.
Agreements reached at the end of a call can be written into a discussion and turned into tasks.

Adherence to a modular architecture + a layered project structure.
A CI pipeline is mandatory.
Access rights are checked not only in HTTP requests but also in websocket events, search, file downloads and AI requests.
After a member is removed from a private channel, they must not keep receiving its new messages over an already open connection.
Resending the same message after a network error must not create duplicates.
Message history must be stored in the DB. A websocket connection is not storage by itself.
Handling of webhooks, reminders and automatic task transitions must account for being run again.
Heavy operations, for example file processing, preparing data for search and AI generation, are run as background jobs.

Logs must not contain integration tokens or the content of private conversations.

Running in production in several instances.
Logging and metrics collection in production are mandatory!
Collecting logs and metrics in production is mandatory.
Storing environment variables — .env for local development, GitHub secrets for CI/CD. We do not commit secrets to the repository.
Maintaining documentation: how to run the project, variables, specifics, etc.
A release to production must be easy and convenient, with one button press in GitHub.
Be sure to check communication and collaboration between users connected to different backend instances.
Be sure to write tests, at least for the core functionality. We are here to learn.
On every pull request, always run linters, tests, the project build and typecheck via ts.
Releases by cutting a branch + pressing the release button in GitHub.
Pushing directly to dev/trunk/master is forbidden, only through a PR with code review.
Working with git using the trunk-based approach.
Containerization is mandatory when deploying.
Cross code review is mandatory. Everyone looks at each other's code, not only the team lead. We learn from other people's code as from our own.
Every week, a report on the work done goes to the chat on Friday. We write the gap even if it is small.
The main task is to build a convenient space for team work.

A user must be able to create a workspace, invite colleagues, set up a project and channels, discuss work, create tasks from conversations and see the result of development through the GitHub integration.
It is important that the features are connected to each other. If chat, Kanban and PR notifications exist separately and do nothing to help the overall process, the project's main task is not solved.

For example, a member writes in a channel about a bug. A task is created from the message and an assignee is appointed. The assignee opens a PR and links it to the task. The team receives a notification, does the review, and after the merge the task moves to the done state. From the task card you can return to the source discussion.

At the same time, the core communication scenarios must work reliably. Messages must not disappear, be duplicated or unexpectedly change order. If sending fails, the user must understand what happened.

Think separately about unread messages. If a person has read a channel on a computer, the counters must update correctly in another open tab too. Also, receiving a message and reading it are different events.
The "online" status also needs attention. One user can open the application in several tabs. Closing one tab must not make them offline if another keeps working.
Direct messages, private channels, tasks and files need clear access rules. A link to an attachment must not let just anyone download a private file.

AI must help work with the accumulated information. The user must be able to verify an answer by opening the source messages, tasks or decisions. If data was changed or deleted, think through how that affects search and AI answers.
Create a workspace → invite a second person → create a project and a channel → exchange messages → create a task from the discussion → bring it to the done state.
Your task is to use AI to the maximum. Development, code review, writing tests, skills, agents, devops, etc., everything your imagination allows.

But do not even try to do everything from one or two prompts. Do not forget about code quality and areas of responsibility. In the early stages of a project, commits of 10k lines of code at a time may get by, but that is a road to nowhere.
Forming the team.
Assigning roles.
Hold the first team call. Get to know each other.
Initialization and basic configuration of the projects.
Set up the basic processes. Decide on the team's internal calls and their times.
Creating boards for work; any can be chosen.
At a high level, the team decomposes the project into logical pieces and blocks that can be developed in parallel.
Before the main development starts, verify message sending between two clients and connection recovery on a small prototype.
Decide on the model of workspaces, projects, channels and access rights.
Get to work.

phases.goal: Any participant clones the repository, runs `docker compose up` (Postgres + pgvector, Redis, S3) and `pnpm dev`, and sees an empty web and api. Every PR automatically passes lint, typecheck, test, build and steiger, gets a first AI review pass, and direct pushes to main are forbidden.
success_criteria: CI is green on main, ruleset enabled (PR + 1 approval + required checks)
The README "how to run" section was verified by two participants on different OSes
CodeRabbit left a comment on a test PR
Versions are pinned exactly per the stack report (TS 6.0.3, Prisma 7.10.1, Next 16.4.5, NestJS 12.4.0)

Users on different instances see each other's messages immediately. Demo 1 shows this in production.

phases.title: Kanban and "My Work" — project board, columns, ordering, realtime, blocking, filters, due dates
phases.goal: Each project has a board with the columns "To do / In progress / In review / Done". Columns can be renamed and added, and cards can be dragged. The order is preserved, changes are immediately visible to everyone, and simultaneous moves do not lose cards. A task can be marked as blocked with a reason, and the assignee gets a notification about assignment, blocking and an approaching due date. "My Work" gathers my tasks from all projects, review requests and mentions.
success_criteria: Two users move cards at the same time — no card is lost or duplicated (test)
The order in a column survives a reload
Filters by assignee, priority and due date work together

phases.title: GitHub — repository connection, webhook verification, PR-to-task link, auto-transitions, PR messages
phases.goal: A project admin connects a repository via the GitHub App and chooses a channel for notifications. Opening a PR with a task key moves the task to "In review", a merge moves it to "Done", and the transitions are visible in the task history. The channel gets one message per PR with the author, title, link and check results. The task card shows the linked PRs. Redelivery of a webhook duplicates nothing, the signature is verified, and data from a private repository is visible only to permitted members. The full spec scenario works from the message to "Done".
success_criteria: E2E: message → task → PR with key → "In review" → merge → "Done" → notification → return to the discussion
Redelivery of the same X-GitHub-Delivery is a no-op (test)
Invalid signature → 401, nothing is saved
Tokens and secrets do not reach the frontend, messages or logs

phases.title: Notifications — notification center, per-channel settings, "Do not disturb", working hours, Telegram bot
phases.goal: A member sees mentions, assigned tasks, thread replies and review requests in a single center and goes from a notification to the specific message, task or PR. Reading in one tab clears the notification in the others. The notification level can be configured per channel and project, and "Do not disturb" and working hours can be turned on, taking the time zone into account. After linking Telegram, reminders about the standup, assignments, mentions and review requests arrive there without duplicates.
success_criteria: A webhook retry and reminders do not create a second notification (UNIQUE dedupe_key)
Outside working hours Telegram is deferred until morning, the in-app notification is there
Telegram linking by deep-link works and can be unlinked from settings
Thread replies and reactions arrive as a digest, not one by one

phases.title: Search, standups and decisions — search with filters, asynchronous standups, team decisions
phases.goal: A member searches the messages of channels available to them with filters by project, channel, author and date and goes to the found message. A project admin configures a standup: schedule, time zone and questions. Members get a reminder and reply in the shared discussion of the day with links to tasks and PRs, it is visible who has already replied, and the history is available to project members. A message or thread can be saved as a decision with a title, description, author, date and a link to the discussion, replaced by a new one with an explanation, and linked to tasks.
success_criteria: A message from a private channel is not found by outsiders (ACL test)
An edited and deleted message is immediately reflected in search
The standup reminder arrives at the set local time exactly once
The "Decisions" tab shows the chain of replacements with history

phases.title: AI assistant — recap, answers with links, tasks from a discussion, summaries, report draft
phases.goal: A member asks for a recap of what they missed in a channel and asks a question about the project ("why did we choose this library?", "what is blocking the release?"). The answer is built only from the messages, tasks and decisions available to them and contains links to sources, and if there is too little data, the AI honestly says so. The generation status is visible: running, done or error. Task suggestions, a decision draft, a project summary and a weekly report draft are saved only after user confirmation. The standup summary contains links to members' replies.
success_criteria: A question about a private channel the user is not in does not reveal its content (test)
Every link in an answer leads to a real accessible source
A deleted message no longer appears in answers
No AI action changes data without confirmation

phases.title: Voice rooms ★ — channel room, microphone, participants and speaker, screen sharing
phases.weeks: W11–W12, only if W10 is green
phases.goal: A channel member joins a voice room, mutes the microphone and leaves. They see who is in the room and who is speaking, and can share their screen. Outsiders cannot get into the room of a private channel. A dropped connection, denied microphone access and the end of screen sharing are handled clearly. During a call the related task can be opened and agreements can be written into the discussion.
success_criteria: An outsider does not get a room token for a private channel
Removal from a channel kicks the user out of the room
